issues.title: This element with an explicit role of listitem is not a child in the accessibility tree of an element with its required context role.
issues.why_it_matters_for_persona: As an autistic person, I rely on clear and predictable structure to understand content. When a list item appears without a list container, it breaks the expected semantic structure. My screen reader might announce 'list item' out of context, which is confusing and makes it harder for me to build a mental model of the page's layout, increasing my cognitive load.
remediation_instructions: Ensure that any element with `role="listitem"` is a direct child of an element with `role="list"`.

Wrap the `
` with `role="listitem"` in a parent `
` with `role="list"`. For example: `
List item 1
`.

Alternatively, use native HTML elements which have these semantics built-in, like `
    ` and `
  • `: `
    • List item 1
    `.
expected_tool_change: An automated accessibility checker will no longer flag this element for having a missing required parent role.
A screen reader will now announce the presence of a list (e.g., 'list, 1 item') before announcing the list item itself, providing proper context.
